perspective:
**Harold Padilla’s available information:**

- He is a project manager. His project is not progressing well, and he initially believes his team is unmotivated. He feels frustrated and anxious.
- He knows Arthur Begum as a trusted friend and police officer and seeks his advice at a coffee shop.
- Harold tells Arthur his team seems unmotivated and it is affecting progress. Arthur says motivation is tricky and asks whether Harold has tried understanding each team member’s individual drives. Harold admits he has focused mostly on project goals and deadlines.
- Arthur advises Harold to have one-on-one conversations and help people feel valued and understood. Harold says he will try and feels more hopeful.
- Afterward, Harold feels relieved and hopeful. He decides to implement Arthur’s advice. He tells his team he wants one-on-one chats to understand what motivates them.
- Team Member 1 says that could be helpful. Team Member 2 says they are open to it. Harold says he will schedule time and wants the project to succeed together.
- Harold later observes that the team still is not responding well. He feels disappointed and worried, so he tells Arthur he tried the suggestions but the team still isn’t responding.
- Arthur says there may be deeper issues, such as personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that Harold may need to dig deeper. Harold decides to hold another round of one-on-one meetings.
- In those meetings, Team Member 1 tells Harold there is tension among a few team members affecting work. Team Member 2 tells Harold they feel overwhelmed by the workload and stressed, making motivation hard.
- Harold says he will look into resolving conflicts, consider redistributing tasks, and cares about their well-being.
- Harold then feels optimistic and empowered. He believes addressing individual concerns will improve team performance and decides to create a more supportive, open environment.
- He tells the team they will have regular feedback sessions and team-building activities. Team Member 1 says that sounds great and will help. Team Member 2 agrees it is good their concerns are being addressed.
- Harold says he is glad and emphasizes that their input and well-being are crucial to the project’s success.
